title: Study of 500 Ice Age spear points reveals how Clovis hunters managed risk
description: A fascinating study delved into the projectile points utilized by ancient Clovis and Cumberland cultures in Tennessee, analyzing nearly 500 artifacts from the late Ice Age. Findings reveal that Clovis groups often resharpened their points due to limited resource knowledge, while Cumberland groups tended to discard points with potential still intact. This suggests an evolving approach to resource management, emphasizing the growing familiarity with their environment over generations.

Why first monsoon drought in 11 years left India dry, and wet
description: The 2026 southwest monsoon is expected to face a significant rainfall deficit across various regions in India. This year's monsoon has been heavily influenced by the strong El Niño phenomenon affecting weather patterns. Many districts in eastern India, including Bihar and parts of the Northeast, are experiencing record low rainfall levels. Simultaneously, the southern regions witness their driest monsoon in over two decades.

title: Australian PM's call to Sam Altman 'reminds' OpenAI to say sorry 90 days after AI hack

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese expressed significant concern regarding the delayed notification and the incident's implications. OpenAI is committing resources to enhance cyber defenses and support affected agencies in Australia.

title: Scientists test 16 Asian elephants with hidden fruit; they learn to follow box
description: In Thailand, Asian elephants demonstrate remarkable adaptability in their feeding behaviors when encountering challenges. Studies indicate that these elephants can switch from direct feeding techniques to indirect methods as needed. While older elephants may find such adaptations more difficult due to slower reflexes, the ability to change tactics is crucial for their social dynamics. This insight into their behavioral flexibility could significantly improve strategies for harmonious coexistence with humans.

title: 1920 Maryland factory restored as business hub with $1 million oyster center

The operation targeted terror launch pads in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in response to the Uri attack. This marked a significant shift towards visible retaliation against terrorism after years of restraint. Similar strategies were applied in subsequent operations like Balakot and Operation Sindoor.

title: Smoking just 1 cigarette a day: Is there a safe number for your heart?
description: Smoking even a small number of cigarettes poses significant risks to cardiovascular health. Research indicates that one cigarette a day can lead to substantial heart disease risks. The cardiovascular dangers persist even when consumption is limited or occasional. Quitting smoking entirely remains the most effective strategy to reduce these risks. Seeking professional help is important for those looking to stop smoking and improve their heart health.

title: Pills, needles, loopholes: Cops battle prescription drug abuse in Chennai
description: A significant rise in prescription drug abuse, particularly Tapentadol and Nitrazepam, is troubling authorities. Police have identified specific injection marks on youths, indicating drug misuse. Despite increased seizures, enforcement laws struggle to address the issue effectively. Traffickers have adapted their methods, moving to underground networks to evade detection. Efforts are ongoing to strengthen the legal framework surrounding these drugs and improve supply chain monitoring.

title: Why Tamil Nadu’s men are dying younger
description: In Tamil Nadu, a considerable difference exists in death rates between men and women across all age groups. Nearly 86% of the excess male deaths occur in younger populations, particularly aged 15 to 64. Risk factors include road crashes and chronic illnesses, which disproportionately affect men. Although health programs exist, they are not organized to effectively reduce male mortality.

title: Bruce Willis built Caribbean compound on 7.3 acres, sold it for $27 million
description: Bruce Willis has finalized the sale of his expansive 7.3-acre beachfront estate on Parrot Cay for a staggering $27 million. Acquired in 2000, the land saw the addition of three custom built homes over four years, nestled within 12 bedrooms and 14 elegant bathrooms. With luxurious outdoor spaces featuring multiple swimming pools, this sale marks a record-breaking residential deal in the Caribbean, as Willis actively streamlines his property portfolio.
